Best prebuilt NAS for Unraid or TrueNAS (2026)

If you're planning to replace the factory OS with Unraid or TrueNAS SCALE, I'd prioritize hardware compatibility, drive expandability, standard SATA connections, and cooling over the NAS manufacturer's software features.

My top choices are:

Best overall: UGREEN NASync DXP6800 Pro — powerful 6-bay hardware, good for an all-in-one home server.

Best compact option: TerraMaster F4-424 Pro — 4-bay Intel-based NAS with strong performance.

Best for TrueNAS: iXsystems TrueNAS Mini — purpose-built for TrueNAS rather than a third-party OS replacement.

Best for expansion: A standard x86 server-style NAS with 8 or more bays, preferably with an HBA and ECC RAM support.

The important distinction: Unraid is more flexible when mixing disk sizes and adding drives over time; TrueNAS is particularly attractive for ZFS storage pools, snapshots, and data integrity.

For a prebuilt NAS that can run either Unraid or TrueNAS, I'd prioritize standard x86 hardware, direct SATA/SAS disk access, good cooling, and the ability to replace or upgrade components.

My top picks are UGREEN NASync, Aoostar, and Minisforum for compact systems, with 45Drives and Supermicro for more serious storage setups.

One important distinction:

Unraid: More flexible with mixed-size drives, excellent Docker support, and easy storage expansion.

TrueNAS SCALE: Better suited to ZFS-focused storage, snapshots, data integrity, and more structured disk configurations.

Avoid buying a NAS solely because it has powerful hardware. Some appliances have locked-down bootloaders, proprietary fan controls, or limited support for installing another OS.

Unraid: Best for mixed-size drives, easy storage expansion, Docker, Plex, and home servers.

TrueNAS SCALE: Best for ZFS, data integrity, snapshots, and more traditional NAS storage. ECC RAM and direct disk access are especially desirable.
